_comment: Example only. The real registry lives at
it holds absolute paths into this host's Hugging Face cache.
A model is rendered one of three ways, checked in this order:
1. cmd     verbatim string or line list; the escape hatch, host-specific
2. engine  named in settings.json; the portable form, preferred
3. neither fall back to the ${server} macro in config.header.yaml
Setting both cmd and engine is an error rather than a silent precedence rule.
Keep tuning here and paths-to-binaries in settings.json. Then the only
per-host delta is settings.json, and sampling/context research travels.
Sampling is deliberately never scaffolded. Vendor presets genuinely
disagree and copying one model's onto another is a real error.

example-vulkan-default._comment: No engine and no cmd: uses the ${server} macro from the header.
example-vulkan-default.description: Why this context, why this sampling, and what was measured to justify them.

_comment: Named engine. The binary, its device pin and -ngl live in settings.json,
so this entry is identical on an AMD box and an NVIDIA one.
'common': false opts out of the ${common} header macro for a model whose
cache types or offload split contradict the shared defaults.
example-engine.description: PQ2_0 is ggml type 142 and needs the PrismML fork; stock llama.cpp cannot load it.

_comment: kind 'custom' engine: not llama.cpp, so no -m/-c/-np are composed.
Only the engine args plus extra_args are passed.
example-custom-engine.description: Own server binary, own flags, exclusive on the GPU.

example-verbatim-cmd._comment: Escape hatch: llama-swap runs this exactly, ${PORT} substituted.
example-verbatim-cmd.description: Prefer an engine; keep this for one-off builds not worth naming.

example-not-served._comment: Only capability 'chat' is rendered into llama-swap.
